question.text: Will the operating rooms of Hospital Privado de Mendoza be open for new surgeries on November 13, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if, as of the end of November 13, 2026 (Mendoza local time, UTC−3), the preventive suspension of surgical activity at the Hospital Privado de Mendoza ordered by the provincial health ministry in October 2026 has been lifted such that the hospital is again authorised to perform new scheduled (non-emergency) operations — including where the lifting is partial or phased, provided at least one of the hospital's operating rooms may again carry out new scheduled surgeries. It resolves NO if the suspension remains fully in force on that date, if only emergency or urgent operations are permitted, or if no credible report indicates any resumption of scheduled surgery at the hospital by then. Resolution is based on announcements from the [Ministerio de Salud y Deportes de Mendoza](https://www.mendoza.gov.ar/salud/), statements by the hospital, or reporting by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions); where reports conflict, provincial health ministry statements govern.
question.fine_print: Evidence that new scheduled operations have in fact been performed at the hospital after the suspension was lifted also counts, even if the ministry issued no formal announcement. The question concerns only the Hospital Privado de Mendoza at Av. Bartolomé Mitre 653, Mendoza city, Argentina.

research:
Short answer: I found no report that the Hospital Privado de Mendoza has reopened its operating rooms or been given a reopening date. The latest coverage I could find (3 November) still describes surgery there as suspended. Nothing settles the question yet.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03: The ministry's page (mendoza.gov.ar/salud) redirects to informacionoficial.mendoza.gob.ar/saludydeportes, and that page returned "403 Forbidden", so I couldn't read official statements directly. Everything below comes from press reports of ministry statements.
- 2026-10-27: Los Andes, using official data up to 26 October, reported that surgery was suspended preventively on 22 October. It gave no reopening criteria or timeline. [Los Andes](https://www.losandes.com.ar/sociedad/diez-pacientes-lupa-el-brote-meningitis-hay-5-infectados-confirmados-y-4-decesos-estudio-n6011981)

## 2. Current status
- The question is not settled. Every report I found from 22 October to 3 November describes surgery at the hospital as suspended.
- 2026-11-03: Los Andes again says the ministry "suspendió preventivamente la actividad quirúrgica" (preventively suspended surgical activity). The article gives no reopening date. [Los Andes](https://www.losandes.com.ar/sociedad/meningitis-el-hospital-privado-un-hombre-entro-operarse-la-cadera-y-lucha-su-vida-n6012696)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Los Andes profiles a patient who had hip surgery on 14 October, got meningitis caused by Serratia marcescens, and is now in intensive care at Hospital Central. Bacterial samples have been sent to the Malbrán Institute (the national reference lab) for genetic typing, to check whether different patients' bacteria are related. I found no published results. [Los Andes](https://www.losandes.com.ar/sociedad/meningitis-el-hospital-privado-un-hombre-entro-operarse-la-cadera-y-lucha-su-vida-n6012696)
- About 2026-10-29/30: Patients' relatives filed the first criminal complaint. Court sources say any charge would fall on individuals, not on the clinic or PAMI. [Salta News](https://www.saltanews.com.ar/mendoza-justicia-investiga-brote-meningitis-denuncia-penal-familiares)
- 2026-10-29: Two more deaths are under investigation in a group of 10 patients, and the operating rooms remain "cerrados preventivamente" (preventively closed). [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/sociedad/2026/10/29/brote-de-meningitis-en-mendoza-investigan-dos-fallecimientos-mas-en-el-hospital-privado/); [La Arena](http://www.laarena.com.ar/la-region/brote-de-meningitis-investigan-dos-fallecimientos-mas-2026102911500)
- 2026-10-28: La Nación reports growing uncertainty about the source of the outbreak and two possible new cases. [La Nación](https://www.lanacion.com.ar/sociedad/brote-de-meningitis-en-mendoza-crece-la-incertidumbre-sobre-el-origen-y-analizan-nuevos-casos-nid28102026/)
- 2026-10-27: 10 patients are under investigation: 5 confirmed, 3 suspected, 2 ruled out. No common source of contamination had been found. Reports said surgery stays suspended until the problems found in the inspections are fixed. [Sitio Andino](https://www.sitioandino.com.ar/salud/brote-meningitis-mendoza-se-confirmo-un-nuevo-caso-y-son-diez-los-pacientes-investigados-n5732665)
- 2026-10-26: Epidemiology director Andrea Falaschi said the operating room must go through "distintas mejoras" (various improvements) before it can work again. The ministry plans a "comprehensive improvement of the surgical process", and sanctions or legal action could follow. [Memo](https://www.memo.com.ar/economia/meningitis-en-el-hospital-privado-salud-investiga-el-origen-del-brote-y-no-descarta-una-contaminacion-en-el-quirofano); [La Nación](https://www.lanacion.com.ar/sociedad/mendoza-en-alerta-por-un-brote-de-meningitis-en-un-hospital-dos-los-cuatro-contagiados-fallecieron-nid26102026/)
- 2026-10-24: Some reports say the hospital's pharmacy was also closed. Antiseptics, anesthetics, medicines and surgical instruments were seized for testing. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/sociedad/2026/10/24/mendoza-cerro-los-quirofanos-de-un-hospital-por-un-brote-de-meningitis-posquirurgica-murieron-dos-pacientes/)
- I found nothing from the hospital itself or from PAMI about reopening or about sending patients elsewhere.

## 4. Base rates
- I found no systematic data on how long Argentine hospitals stay closed after an outbreak.
- One loose comparison from the news feed: a hospital in Lleida, Spain, reopened six operating rooms on 3 November, 11 days after a water-leak closure on 23 October, once cleaning was done and microbiology cultures came back negative. [El Periódico](https://www.elperiodico.com/es/sanidad/20261102/hospital-arnau-reabre-quirofanos-136008354) That case had no deaths, no unknown source and no criminal case.
- Here, several things point to a longer closure, though this is my reading rather than a sourced finding:
  - the source is still unidentified
  - the genetic typing results are still pending
  - officials want process-wide improvements first
  - there are up to 4 possible deaths
  - a criminal investigation is open
- Day 22 after the suspension is 13 November.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the collected Kalshi markets match this question. They are about hotel rooms, football, the NFL and similar topics.
- I found no Polymarket, Manifold or Metaculus forecast on it.

## 6. Upcoming events before 13 November
- Malbrán typing results could identify a common source or a contaminated product.
- Results of the operating-room cultures and samples could come in.
- The ministry may sign off on the required improvements and authorise a partial or phased reopening.
- Developments in the criminal case or new confirmed deaths could prolong the closure.
- The case count could change: patients operated on in September and October are still under follow-up.

I could not find any report that the operating rooms have reopened. The latest coverage, up to a Los Andes story on 3 Nov, still describes surgery at the hospital as suspended. No reopening date or timetable has been announced.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03: I could not find a ministry press release about this outbreak on mendoza.gov.ar. Searches of that site only returned unrelated hospital news, so the ministry's position comes through media quotes.
- 2026-10-27 (case counts as of 10-26): The ministry says 10 patients are under investigation: 5 confirmed *Serratia marcescens*, 3 suspected and 2 ruled out. It says the four deaths should not all be attributed to the bacterium yet, and that surgeries "se encuentran suspendidas" (are suspended). [Los Andes](https://www.losandes.com.ar/sociedad/diez-pacientes-lupa-el-brote-meningitis-hay-5-infectados-confirmados-y-4-decesos-estudio-n6011981)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-11-03: Nothing settles the question yet. The latest article (Los Andes, 3 Nov) still says surgical activity is suspended as a precaution. The bacterial samples have been sent to the Instituto Malbrán, the national reference laboratory, and no source of contamination has been officially confirmed. [Los Andes](https://www.losandes.com.ar/sociedad/meningitis-el-hospital-privado-un-hombre-entro-operarse-la-cadera-y-lucha-su-vida-n6012696)
- Several searches for "reabren", "rehabilitan" or "retoma" (reopen, re-authorise, resume) found no report of scheduled surgery restarting.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Profile of patient Carlos Bordón, who had a hip operation on 14 Oct and is still fighting for his life. His daughters filed a criminal complaint, and the prosecutor's office (Unidad Fiscal Correccional) asked the hospital for his medical records. There is no official confirmation of a sterilisation failure. [Los Andes](https://www.losandes.com.ar/sociedad/meningitis-el-hospital-privado-un-hombre-entro-operarse-la-cadera-y-lucha-su-vida-n6012696)
- 2026-10-29: The operating rooms are "cerrados preventivamente" (closed as a precaution). Two more deaths are under study but have no microbiological confirmation. Samples went to Malbrán for genotyping, and no common source has been established. Epidemiology director Andrea Falaschi said investigators are looking at anaesthetics, infusions and other surgical materials, the building's condition, patient routes into the operating rooms, and how patients are prepared. Neither the ministry nor the hospital mentioned a reopening timeline. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/sociedad/2026/10/29/brote-de-meningitis-en-mendoza-investigan-dos-fallecimientos-mas-en-el-hospital-privado/), [La Arena](https://www.laarena.com.ar/la-region/brote-de-meningitis-investigan-dos-fallecimientos-mas-2026102911500)
- 2026-10-28: Uncertainty about the origin is growing, and two possible new cases are being analysed. [La Nación](https://www.lanacion.com.ar/sociedad/brote-de-meningitis-en-mendoza-crece-la-incertidumbre-sobre-el-origen-y-analizan-nuevos-casos-nid28102026/)
- 2026-10-26: Falaschi said the operating room needs "several improvements" before it can work again. She did not say what they are or give a timeline. [Memo](https://www.memo.com.ar/economia/meningitis-en-el-hospital-privado-salud-investiga-el-origen-del-brote-y-no-descarta-una-contaminacion-en-el-quirofano)
- ~2026-10-24: Besides the operating rooms, the hospital pharmacy was reportedly closed, and antiseptics, anaesthetics and instruments were seized for testing. [C5N](https://www.c5n.com/sociedad/brote-fatal-meningitis-mendoza-cerraron-los-quirofanos-un-hospital-privado-la-muerte-dos-pacientes-n252471)
- 2026-10-22: The ministry ordered the precautionary suspension until the investigation concludes. One outlet says the hospital itself had stopped surgery a day earlier, on Tuesday. [El Sol](https://www.elsol.com.ar/mendoza/suspendieron-las-cirugias-en-el-hospital-privado-por-un-brote-de-meningitis-posquirurgica/), [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/sociedad/2026/10/24/mendoza-cerro-los-quirofanos-de-un-hospital-por-un-brote-de-meningitis-posquirurgica-murieron-dos-pacientes/)

## 4. Base rates
- I found no systematic data on how long operating rooms stay closed after an outbreak.
- Similar cases:
  - Ibiza: the Can Misses hospital reopened six operating rooms after an insect problem, once microbiological tests came back negative. [Mallorcadiario](https://www.mallorcadiario.com/can-misses-abre-los-seis-quirofanos-cerrados-por-el-foco-de-moscas)
  - Lleida: the Arnau de Vilanova hospital closed six operating rooms on 23 Oct 2026 over a water leak and planned to reopen them on 3 Nov after negative cultures, about 11 days. [El Periódico](https://www.elperiodico.com/es/sanidad/20261102/hospital-arnau-reabre-quirofanos-136008354)
  - Durango, Mexico (2022-23): after a fatal meningitis outbreak in women given epidural anaesthesia at private hospitals, the closures lasted much longer, months, and came with court cases. [Vanguardia](https://vanguardia.com.mx/noticias/24-mujeres-tienen-meningitis-en-durango-clausuran-quirofanos-de-hospital-privado-YF5007616)
- My reading: closures for a simple environmental problem tend to last 1 to 3 weeks. Closures after a fatal outbreak, especially with a criminal case and an unidentified source, tend to last longer. By 13 Nov, the Mendoza closure will be about 22 days old.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the markets supplied (Kalshi: Wyndham and Marriott hotel rooms, Godoy Cruz vs Rivadavia football, Fernando Mendoza's NFL start, the US gas tax, and others) relate to this question.
- I found no Polymarket, Manifold, Metaculus community or expert forecast on this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Malbrán genotyping results, which would show whether the cases are linked or point to a single contaminated product.
- Lab results on the seized antiseptics, anaesthetics and instruments, and whether the pharmacy closure is lifted.
- Whether the hospital completes the "improvements" Falaschi said were needed, followed by a ministry re-inspection.
- Whether the two suspected deaths are confirmed or any new cases appear, either of which would likely extend the closure.
- Possible orders from the prosecutor in the criminal case.
- Pressure from PAMI, the retirees' health fund: the hospital is described as its main provider in Mendoza, so the suspension backs up surgery for pensioners. [El Monterizo](https://www.elmonterizo.com/el-quirofano-que-no-cierra-cinco-contagiados-y-dos-muertos-en-un-hospital-de-mendoza)

Note: my searches returned nothing published between 30 Oct and 2 Nov, so I may have missed developments from those days.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain, until the end of 13 November 2026 (Mendoza time). For Yes, the ministry must lift the preventive surgical suspension, at least partially, so that at least one operating room can do new scheduled operations. Credible evidence that scheduled surgeries have actually resumed would also count. Reopening for emergency surgery only does not count.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. The operating rooms have been closed since 22 October, and every report through 3 November describes them as still suspended. No reopening date has been announced.

(c) Base rate: there is little systematic data. My loose reference class is hospital operating-room closures after an infection outbreak or contamination event, and whether they reopen within about 3 weeks.
- Closures for simple environmental causes, with no deaths and a known cause (for example, the Lleida water leak), often reopen within 1 to 2 weeks.
- Closures with deaths, an unidentified source and legal or criminal scrutiny usually last longer, often a month or more.
- A blended estimate for "reopened within 22 days" in cases like this one is about 25 to 30%.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - Officials see a contaminated item as the leading hypothesis (26 October). If it is confirmed as a product batch, replacing the product and fixing protocols could allow a fairly quick reopening.
  - The outbreak had not spread further as of 26 October.
  - A private hospital that serves PAMI has strong financial and patient-access pressure to resume surgery.
  - The ministry's conditions are framed as "improvements", which can be done within weeks.
- For No:
  - On 3 November surgery was still suspended, with no timeline.
  - The source was still unidentified as of 27-28 October, and the Malbrán genetic typing results are pending.
  - Up to 4 deaths are possible (29 October), and a criminal complaint has been filed (about 30 October).
  - The pharmacy was also reportedly closed (24 October).
  - Officials want a "comprehensive improvement of the surgical process" (26 October).
  - Regulators facing deaths and media scrutiny tend to be cautious.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: The Malbrán results are slow or inconclusive, or new cases or deaths are confirmed. The ministry keeps the operating rooms closed through mid-November while the hospital carries out the required changes and the courts proceed.
- Yes: Around 6 to 10 November, the lab identifies a contaminated antiseptic or medication batch from an outside supplier. The hospital replaces its supplies and resubmits protocols, environmental cultures come back negative, and the ministry authorises a phased reopening of one or two operating rooms before 13 November.

(f) I start from about 27% and move slightly down to about 22%. As of today, 12 days into the closure, there is no sign of progress toward reopening. The investigation is still open-ended, with pending typing results and a criminal case, and only 10 days remain. I keep the forecast well above single digits because a product-contamination finding could quickly lead to a phased reopening, and the hospital has strong pressure to resume.

Probability: 22%

(a) About 10 days remain, until the end of 13 November 2026 Mendoza time. For Yes, the ministry must lift the preventive suspension ordered on 22 October, at least partially, so that one or more operating rooms may again perform new scheduled (non-emergency) surgery. Alternatively, credible reports must show that scheduled surgeries have resumed.

(b) The status quo is No. Surgical activity has been suspended since 22 October, and every report through 3 November describes it as still suspended, with no reopening date announced.

(c) Base rate: preventive operating-room closures after a hospital-acquired infection outbreak usually last from about two weeks to a couple of months. Simple environmental problems, such as the Lleida water leak, can clear in about 11 days. Outbreaks with deaths, an unidentified source and pending reference-lab typing tend to take longer. Examples include clinic restrictions after the 2022 Tucumán Legionella outbreak, which lasted roughly a month or more. For a closure reaching about 22 days in this harder class, I estimate roughly 25-30% reopen by then.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - The leading hypothesis is a contaminated surgical item (26 October). If confirmed, the item could be replaced quickly and the fixes certified.
  - The outbreak had not spread further as of 26 October.
  - Officials have framed reopening as conditional on specific improvements, not as an indefinite closure.
  - There is financial and capacity pressure, since the hospital is a PAMI provider.
- For No:
  - As of 3 November, Los Andes still reports the suspension, with no timeline given.
  - Malbrán genetic typing results are pending.
  - The source is still unidentified (27-28 October).
  - Up to 4 deaths are under investigation (29 October).
  - A criminal complaint was filed around 29-30 October.
  - The ministry wants a "comprehensive improvement of the surgical process" (26 October).
  - The pharmacy was reportedly also closed.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: the Malbrán results arrive slowly or are inconclusive. New suspected cases or deaths keep political pressure high. The ministry keeps the operating rooms closed through mid-November while the hospital completes its required protocol changes and new environmental cultures come back.
- Yes: the typing points to a single contaminated antiseptic or anesthetic lot. The hospital replaces its supplies, revises its sterilisation protocols and gets negative cultures. Around 10-12 November, the ministry authorises a phased reopening of one or two operating rooms for scheduled cases.

(f) I start at about 27%. I move down slightly because, as of day 12 of the closure, there is no sign of any progress toward reopening: no identified source, pending lab results, an open criminal case and a rising death toll. These make officials cautious. Against that, a product-contamination finding could produce a quick conditional reopening, and partial reopening counts as Yes. My final estimate is about 20%.

Probability: 20%

(a) About 10 days remain, until the end of November 13, 2026 (Mendoza time). For Yes, the Mendoza health ministry must lift the October 22 preventive suspension at least partially, so that at least one operating room may again perform new scheduled (non-emergency) surgeries. Credible reports that scheduled surgeries have actually resumed also count. Permission for emergency surgery only does not count.

(b) The status quo is No. Surgery has been suspended since October 22. As of November 3 every report still describes it as suspended, and no reopening date has been given.

(c) Base rate: after a fatal post-surgical outbreak with an unidentified source, operating-room closures usually last several weeks to months. They reopen once the source is found, corrective works are verified and environmental cultures come back negative. Closures caused by simple contamination events without deaths can reopen in about 10 to 14 days (Lleida: 11 days). Weighting toward the fatal, unexplained-source class, roughly 20-25% of such closures lift within about 3 weeks.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- The hospital is private and a PAMI provider, so it has strong financial and patient-access pressure to reopen.
- On October 26 officials framed reopening as conditional on "improvements", which can sometimes be done quickly.
- On October 26 Falaschi said the outbreak had not spread further.
- The ministry could authorise a phased reopening once audits are passed.

Evidence for No:
- As of October 27 to November 3 the source was still unidentified, and Malbrán genetic typing was pending on November 3.
- Up to 4 deaths, with two more under investigation since October 29.
- A criminal complaint was filed around October 29 to 30.
- On October 26 the ministry called for a "comprehensive improvement of the surgical process".
- On October 24 the pharmacy reportedly closed too and supplies were seized.
- No reopening timeline exists as of November 3.

(e) No scenario: Malbrán results arrive slowly or point to a systemic process failure. The ministry requires infrastructure and protocol changes and then verification cultures, so the closure runs into late November or December amid political sensitivity over the deaths.

Yes scenario: Testing identifies a single contaminated batch of antiseptic or anaesthetic. The hospital replaces its supplies and protocols, and inspectors approve a phased reopening of one operating room around November 10 to 13, which local media report.

(f) I start from roughly 22% and adjust slightly down. The criminal case and the unknown source make regulators cautious, and Yes requires both the decision and the reporting within 10 days. Offsetting this, the hospital's financial pressure and the fact that the closure was explicitly labelled "preventive" leave a real chance of an early partial reopening.
